newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan store sales quite steady in July - MITI.
newsitem.headline: Japan store sales quite steady in July - MITI.

text.p: Sales at Japan's supermarkets and department stores were quite steady in July, according to preliminary data, Vice Trade Minister Osamu Watanabe told reporters on Monday.
He said that, although sales had been poor in June, information received from stores on a daily basis had shown that sales were steady in July.
He added, however, that domestic car sales in July had been a little disappointing, falling 10.1 percent year-on-year.
Watanabe said he had heard that there were many customers coming into showrooms, but they were not ready yet to make purchases.

He said he expected replacement demand to emerge later in the year as customers would be encouraged to buy new cars instead of having their older cars go through Japan's rigorous and expensive inspection system.

"We are not necessarily pessimistic about sales from the autumn, but July sales can be seen as one example of where the reaction to the rise in the sales tax has spilled over past June," he said, adding that he was very interested in watching movements in the car sector.

Asked about inventory levels, he said that although stock levels rose in the April-June period, this had followed large drops in the January-March period as consumers rushed to buy goods before the sales tax went up on April 1.
"The April-to-June levels were higher, but I do not think these levels are extremely high," he said.
